text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- The Swiss government decided that provisionally admitted Bosnian refugees must leave Switzerland by April 30, 1997. Young people and families with children may stay longer.
- Switzerland's lower house of parliament voted in favour of a new value-added tax law.
- After nine months of evaluation and development, some 200 Swiss libraries now have been connected to the Internet. Internet users have access to more than 7.1 million entries.
- Swiss border officials said they registered no increase in the number of Albanians attempting to cross the Swiss border illegally.
- Police cleared a railway track leading to a Swiss nuclear power station. Greenpeace activists had blocked the track to stop the transport of nuclear waste.
- Swiss travel group Kuoni reported a 20.5 percent increase in 1996 sales, 10.4 percent of the increase was due to acquisitions. Net profit rose 53.5 percent to 69.4 million Swiss francs.
- The Swiss National Bank presented exact figures on its gold transactions during World War Two. The report shows the same figures that had already been published in 1946.
- The universities of Lausanne and Geneva announced strategic cooperation plans aimed at achieving a better position in the international and European education market.
